Review against the #255 regression found by a real seeded run. At default haiku/$1, whole-unit coverage fell from 30+13 to 16+7, with 20 units "not reached", while only $0.42 was spent and no hint was shown.

- **Root cause:** the collector's K (`unitCalls`) ignored the block-call reserve, so the engine's pre-flight dropped unit rooms 4–5. Those rooms held only second-or-later parts, but `droppedUnits` recorded whole unit ids. Units already reviewed in part were then reported as not reached.
- **Fix:** the collector runs the engine's own pre-flight (`keptRooms`) and re-plans to the K the engine will keep. First-fit is a prefix, so first parts stay first. Drops are recorded per part, and a unit with a surviving part counts as reached. Dropped parts get a visible line. The lead table cap is now 20, with unreferenced exports first.
- **The crash my gate caught on the first real run is fixed:** a TDZ error where `run()` reached `const pricePart` before it was initialised. A new test runs the engine as a script through the split path. Adapter exceptions are now class `internal` and always red, so a bug of ours can't hide behind a green check on a weekly scan.
- **Real seeded run (Kite 39001362367, default settings):** 43/43 reviewed (30 whole + 13 forced, 0 not reached), against 23 before. Cost is the same ($0.42), the run took 4m40s against 4m33s, and the `moveCrop`/`pointerNote` leads are now visible. Recall is unchanged (model 3/8, static 6/8, combined 6/8), as expected, since this PR restores coverage rather than adding detection.
- The dogfood's two "assertion removed" findings (audit-post.test.js:994-995) are the old cap-of-10 assertions, deliberately replaced. They are false positives.

LGTM. One note inline; merging.
